title: Polls open in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – UK politics live
summary:
Voters choosing replacement for Keir Starmer, who announced he was standing down last month

The French finance minister, Roland Lescure, said the UK could rejoin the EU…

items: 25m agoVoters go to the polls in Holborn and St Pancras byelection

blocks.text: The French finance minister, Roland Lescure, said the UK could rejoin the EU “anytime” after Andy Burnham indicated a major review of Britain’s relationship with the bloc.
Lescure said it was up to the British public whether to return to the EU, telling the BBC that “if they’re willing to come back, they will have to decide”.
“But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime,” he added. Ben Quinn has the full report here.

blocks.caption: France’s finance minister Roland Lescure said the UK should rejoin the EU ‘anytime’. Photograph: Kenzo Tribouillard/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: As our political correspondent Aletha Adu reported last week, the prime minister opened the door to the UK rejoining the EU, saying Britain could “go all the way” as he prepares to reconsider Labour’s post-Brexit red lines.
Voters go to the polls in Holborn and St Pancras byelection
Good morning and welcome to our UK politics live blog.
Polls have opened in Keir Starmer’s old seat in Holborn and St Pancras, where the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, is hoping to break Labour’s longstanding grip in the north London constituency.

blocks.caption: A dog is led towards a polling station as voting begins in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images

blocks.text: He might have his work cut out for him. Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali is projected to retain the seat in today’s byelection, but the party shouldn’t take victory for granted. As the Guardian’s senior political correspondent, Peter Walker, reports, Polanski has mounted an intensive campaign, but the scale of the challenge is clear from the numbers. Starmer won the seat by 11,500 votes in 2024, after Labour majorities of nearly 28,000 in 2019 and more than 30,500 in 2017.

items: Andy Burnham is in Berlin today where he will hold meetings with German chancellor Friedrich Merz. On the agenda is a new joint security partnership to counter sabotage, cyber-attacks and other hybrid threats, as well as support for Ukraine, instability in the Middle East, and disruption to global trade routes. We’re expecting to hear from the prime minister this afternoon.

The diplomatic row between Britain and Israel is escalating over the UK’s consular presence in East Jerusalem. Israel said the British consulate has “ceased to function” with 20 diplomats due to leave, but the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said the building will remain open and renamed the “UK Mission”.
